title: Nasruddin Tale 186: The Foreign Ambassador
summary: A foreign ambassador arrived who spoke only through signs. He drew a circle in the sand. Nasruddin drew a line across it. The ambassador held up three fingers; Nasruddin held up on...
full_text:
A foreign ambassador arrived who spoke only through signs. He drew a circle in the sand. Nasruddin drew a line across it. The ambassador held up three fingers; Nasruddin held up one. The ambassador held up an egg; Nasruddin held up an onion.

The ambassador bowed in deep awe: "Your scholar is a supreme genius! I showed him the earth; he showed me the equator! I showed him the three realms; he showed me divine unity! I showed him cosmic mystery; he showed me the layers of creation!"

After the envoy departed, the Sultan asked Nasruddin: "What did you say to him?"

Nasruddin laughed: "He showed me a round flatbread; I said I would cut it in half! He said he would eat three slices; I said I would eat the whole thing! Then he pulled out a boiled egg for lunch, and I showed him an onion to season it with!"
moral: Grand diplomatic gestures often conceal ordinary human appetites.
